name: SparkleDB
tagline: Norwegian semantic (RDF/SPARQL) NoSQL database marketed for big data around 2012-2015; now defunct.
description: SparkleDB was a commercial semantic database from SparkleDB AS (associated with SysSurge AS) that promised a horizontally scalable, transactional RDF store queried with SPARQL, with automatic sharding, replication without a single point of failure, persistent or in-memory operation and TLS-secured access on Windows, macOS and Linux. Its website asked visitors to request a beta invite and went offline after 2015; no public releases, source code or independent evaluations survive. It is listed for completeness. For SPARQL workloads, use one of the established RDF stores.
statusNote: Website offline since about 2015 and no releases survive. For SPARQL use Virtuoso, GraphDB, Stardog or Apache Jena.

pricing.notes: Pricing was never published; the product is no longer available.

scale.notes: Automatic sharding and replication were vendor claims that were never independently verified.

strengths: Aimed to combine SPARQL querying with automatic sharding and replication
Could run as a persistent or in-memory store, according to the vendor
weaknesses: Proprietary, so nothing can be recovered or forked
useCases: Example of early-2010s scale-out RDF store marketing
